name: mdx-learning-implicit-signal-contract
purpose: Define Learn's implicit signal capture: the zero-user-cost learning source the frontier mines. A human never assembles these. They are derived from dispositions the product already records - a Forge change accepted, rejected, sent back for revision, or edited right after an accept, and a Twin answer a person marked as not right - and each cites the exact disposition receipt it was derived from in the ledger. A rejection and an edit-after-accept are the highest-signal disagreement classes. The signal drafts a candidate lesson the human still gates; nothing here activates memory or adapts behavior.

signal_kinds.meaning: A human accepted a Forge-produced change as produced. The quieter signal, but it teaches what ships cleanly.
A human rejected a Forge-produced change. A high-signal disagreement: this kind of change on this kind of work needs a different approach.
A human sent a change back for revision before it could ship.
A change was revised right after it was accepted. A high-signal disagreement: the accept missed something the edit caught.
A person marked a Twin answer as not right. The choice-as-labeling signal.

fold: each learning.implicit.signal receipt folds into a DRAFTED candidate lesson in the /learning/forge-outcome-candidates/projection.json lane, deduped against judged and rejected candidates and sanitized by the same instruction-injection scan as every other rail. The human is still the only gate.
